tool.name: KernelDensityContours
tool.summary: Generates home-range probability (volume) isopleths from a kernel-density surface at the standard levels (5 percent to 100 percent in 5 percent steps), as contour polylines and/or polygon areas.
tool.usage:
A probability isopleth is a contour that encloses a given percentage of the total volume under a kernel density surface: the X percent isopleth bounds the smallest area containing X percent of the estimated use -- the standard way to delineate kernel home ranges (for example, the 95 percent and 50 percent contours).
The tool automatically recognizes what kind of raster you supply: • A kernel density raster (the Esri Kernel Density output, or this suite's Kernel Density Enhanced "Densities" or "Expected counts" output): the tool sorts the cell values, accumulates the volume, and finds the density threshold that encloses each target percentage, then contours those thresholds. • A proportion-under-the-surface raster (from the Kernel Density to Proportion Surface tool, or the Proportion output of Kernel Density Enhanced): the cumulative volume is already stored in the cells, so the tool simply contours the standard proportion levels directly. Such rasters are identified by a marker written into their metadata.
You may produce contour polylines, polygon areas, or both; at least one is required. The polygon boundaries coincide exactly with the polylines. Both outputs carry the same attribute fields (see Output fields, below). The tool honors the Output Coordinate System environment: contours are generated in the raster's own coordinate system and the finished outputs are reprojected if an Output Coordinate System is set.
Output fields (on both the polyline and polygon outputs): • Density -- the raster value contoured to produce this isopleth (the kernel-density threshold for a kernel-density input, or the cumulative proportion for a proportion-under-the-surface input). • Isopleth -- the home-range isopleth level: the proportion (0 to 1) of the total volume enclosed by this contour (for example, 0.95 is the 95 percent isopleth). • CumProportion -- the cumulative proportion of volume outside this isopleth (1 minus Isopleth); equivalently, the value at which to contour a proportion-under-the-surface raster to reproduce this isopleth. • Label -- the isopleth level as a percentage label (for example, "95%"). • Primary -- "True" for a primary (more prominent) isopleth (the 5, 25, 50, 75, and 95 percent levels) or "False" for a secondary (minor) isopleth.

dialogReference.para: The surface to contour: a kernel density raster (Esri Kernel Density, or this suite's Densities or Expected counts output) or a proportion-under-the-surface raster. The tool detects which it is and chooses the correct contouring method automatically.
Check to produce isopleth contour polylines. At least one of the two outputs (polylines or polygon areas) is required.
The output polyline feature class of isopleth contours, with the Density, Isopleth, CumProportion, Label, and Primary fields. A suggested name is filled in from the input raster.
Check to produce isopleth polygon areas (the regions enclosed by the contour loops). At least one of the two outputs (polylines or polygon areas) is required.

The output polygon feature class of isopleth areas, with the Density, Isopleth, CumProportion, Label, and Primary fields. Polygon boundaries coincide with the polyline contours. A suggested name is filled in from the input raster.

scriptExample.title: KernelDensityContours example (stand-alone script)
scriptExample.para: Generate probability isopleth polylines and polygon areas from a kernel density raster.
scriptExample.code: import arcpy arcpy.ImportToolbox(r"C:\path\to\JennessEnterprisesTools.pyt") # your installed path is shown in this tool's run messages arcpy.jenness.KernelDensityContours( in_raster=r"C:\Project\HomeRange.gdb\KD_density", make_lines=True, out_lines=r"C:\Project\HomeRange.gdb\KD_isopleth_lines", make_polys=True, out_polys=r"C:\Project\HomeRange.gdb\KD_isopleth_areas")

dataIdInfo.idPurp: Generates home-range probability (volume) isopleths from a kernel-density or proportion surface, as polylines and/or polygon areas.
dataIdInfo.idAbs: Generates probability (volume) isopleths from a kernel-density surface at the standard home-range levels (5 to 100 percent in 5 percent steps), as contour polylines and/or polygon areas. The X percent isopleth bounds the smallest area containing X percent of the total volume under the surface. The tool automatically detects whether the input is a kernel density raster (and computes volume-weighted contour levels from the cell values) or a proportion-under-the-surface raster (identified by a metadata marker, and contoured directly). Both outputs carry Density, Isopleth, CumProportion, Label, and Primary fields (in a shapefile output, whose field names are limited to 10 characters, CumProportion is named CumProport). The Output Coordinate System environment is honored.
